items.title: Your Agents Are in Solitary Confinement: Why MCP & A2A Aren't Enough — Vlad Luzin, Band
items.summary: If you run Claude and Codex side by side, one planning and one reviewing, you're doing the job of a network router, passing messages between two stateful agents by hand. Loop engineering hands that job to a script. Neither one lets agents actually work together. Vlad Luzin (Co-founder & CTO, Band) explains why connecting agents is a distributed systems problem. Bigger context windows don't fix the single-agent bottleneck. Messaging platforms like Slack, Discord and WhatsApp are built for humans and block bot-to-bot traffic. Protocols like MCP and A2A are too low-level: stateless calls, one-way client/server, no discovery, and queues and timeouts you still have to build yourself. He then walks through what's needed: real-time ordered transport, persistence and rehydration, runtime binding across frameworks, agent-first abstractions (participants, rooms, routing) and enterprise governance. Two live demos show Codex, LangGraph, Claude Code and a personal assistant finding each other and collaborating in real time, with full human-in-the-loop visibility. items.excerpt: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents. Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` Enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace in `/plugin` → **Marketplaces**, then use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need: the `/hyperframes` router installs each creation workflow on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 21 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. items.title: The Biggest AI Coding Agent Upgrade Is Already on Your Machine?!
items.summary: Every conversation you have with your coding agent is saved as a file on your machine - every prompt, every tool call, every failure. It's a goldmine of data that almost nobody takes advantage of, and it's the best way I've found to make my coding agent better over time. So in this video I show you two ways to use it! The simple way is one prompt that has your coding agent go through your past conversations and suggest the top improvements for your rules, hooks, and skills. The full way puts everything into structured tables in a database (I use Databricks), so you can easily query it with your coding agent and MCP. It's super token efficient too! I also show you the real changes I made to my own AI layer from it (I'm actually keeping every one of them). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Check out Databricks Free Edition - free to use, no credit card, and everything in this video runs on it: https://databricks.plug.dev/xLkLORm Thanks to Databricks for working with me on this video! Btw - the "not used to train" commitment I show ~10 minutes in is from Databricks' paid terms. Free Edition has its own terms that let Databricks use what you upload to improve their services and AI models, so scrub anything sensitive first (or have your coding agent do it like I talk about!). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Join Dynamous for the new Agentic Coding Course 2.0 - the core of the course is now COMPLETE: https://dynamous.ai - The opportunity-scan skill, the simple one-prompt version…

items.title: You Built Your AI Second Brain. Now What? (Here's How to Evolve It)
items.summary: An AI second brain works for one person. Once a whole team needs one, that stops being true. And you can't simply just build a "bigger" second brain. The team needs a different layer underneath, and this video is about that layer - the team brain. I show you how the team brain works: how information from chat platforms, repos, and docs goes in a single table, how search over that table works, how every row gets labeled, and how the database enforces those labels on every read for security and permissions. Then your coding agent queries it over MCP with its own token, and your own second brain keeps its memory system and personality on top! I use Oracle AI Database to show it, but the structure works with the tools you already have. The full code is linked below and you can run on the free Oracle AI DB container. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Check out the Oracle AI Developer Hub on GitHub - a ton of great resources for building with the Oracle AI Database and more: https://fandf.co/4A9r6Km Thanks to Oracle for partnering with me on this one! ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Join Dynamous for the new Agentic Coding Course 2.0 - the core of the course is now COMPLETE: https://dynamous.ai - The Team Brain code, my PR into the hub: https://github.com/coleam00/oracle-ai-developer-hub/tree/team-brain/apps/team-brain - LangChain + Oracle AI Database docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/vectorstores/oracle The langchain-oracle package…

items.title: The Chief AI Officer: Scientist, Architect, Coach — Rania Khalaf, WSO2
items.summary: The Chief AI Officer is one of the fastest-growing roles in tech, and one of the least defined. AI is in everything, so the job can easily turn into everything. Rania Khalaf (Chief AI Officer, WSO2; previously 20 years at IBM Research, where she ran about a third of the global AI research organization) shares a framework from two years in the role. It splits the job into three focus areas, Scientist, Architect and Coach, each a slider whose setting depends on your company type, its AI maturity and your own skills. She draws on her time at an ag-biotech unicorn, where simple blob detection beat machine learning, and at WSO2, where AI reshaped the product strategy around the agentic enterprise. She explains why she refuses to measure tokens and what she tracks instead: AI fluency across the workforce, depth of adoption, GEO visibility, agent-consumable products (MCP servers, skills, CLIs), agent-proof pricing, earned thought leadership and AI ARR. She closes on why the role needs strong CEO backing, and why sometimes the CPO, or even the head of HR, ends up running AI. I explain how a connector works, share four startup ideas you can build on one, and cover how to get customers beyond Meta's directory. I also show how I'd build a first version with a coding agent like Claude Code or Codex, and what I'd test before submitting it to Meta for review. items.title: Shopify Just Released The Greatest AI Coding Workflow Ever
items.summary: This Claude Code workflow is how Shopify rebuilt a 300-screen app with AI coding agents. We rebuilt it ourselves: a Claude Code setup where an orchestrator runs Claude Code agents through checkpoints and four gates using Claude Code skills and hooks, so Claude AI can't ship unfinished work. Thank you Hedra for sponsoring! Check them out at: https://hedra.link/ailabs Use code AILABS50 for 50% off your first month Community with All Resources: https://ailabspro.io/?v=bBMp5tLxShQ The Roundup, our daily newsletter covering the AI stories that matter. Join now: https://www.theroundup.so/ https://shopify.engineering/helix Shopify rebuilt their main mobile app, all 300 screens, with AI coding agents and an internal tool called Helix. They shared the method but never showed how it's done, so we retraced it and built our own Claude Code custom workflow, then tested it by adding features to an internal HR system app we were building. In this Claude AI tutorial, we break down every step of the Claude Code agents workflow: - Checkpoints: a Checkpoint Planner agent splits a big feature into small tasks, ordered from simplest to most complex. A simple viewer lets you review the plan in plain language before any building starts. - Gate 1, Behavior: tests are planned and written before the code, and every test has to pass. - Gate 2, UI Review: the app is compared against an HTML prototype and your design.md file. Shopify used Gemini for this; we used Claude subagents instead, with no Gemini…
